title: ChatGPT-3.5 alongside instructional videos raises dental students' simulated operative skill scores in a 187-student randomized trial in China
summary: In a 2024 randomized trial with 187 dental undergraduates in China, students who used ChatGPT-3.5 with instructional videos scored 73.12 against 65.54 on a virtual reality skills test.
account: Researchers at the School and Hospital of Stomatology, Wuhan University, recruited 192 undergraduate dental students at a Chinese university by 25 October 2024. After eye-tracking calibration, 187 students were randomly assigned by sealed envelopes to learn a clinical operative skill from videos alone or from the same videos with the free ChatGPT-3.5, and all finished the protocol by 2 November 2024. During a one-week learning period the ChatGPT group could ask about doubts and check procedural steps. Both groups were then tested on a desktop virtual reality simulator. The ChatGPT group scored 73.12 against 65.54 for the video-only group (P < .001) and showed lower cognitive load on eye-tracking measures. Students with low spatial ability gained most, 70.20 against 55.41, and the difference among students with high spatial ability was not significant. The authors note that the comparison group had no added support and that they could not check the accuracy of the answers that ChatGPT gave. The Journal of Medical Internet Research published the study on 27 May 2025.
purpose: ChatGPT is a general-purpose chatbot. The authors tested it as a skills instructor, and better skill performance was the purpose of the trial.
